comment: Flask on gunicorn, one blueprint per family under Implementation/routes. gunicorn runs two worker processes, because one Python process runs Python on one core at a time and the container has two, with the gthread worker, because the sync worker closes the connection after every answer. On lambda-emulator the application answers behind apig-wsgi, in one process. No framework document or client: Flask writes no OpenAPI document without a third-party library. The suite is UnitTests/, pytest over Flask's test client, and never reaches the image. The suite and upgrade run through uv, which has to be installed.

unsupported.sse.medium: apig-wsgi buffers the whole answer, so the events arrive as one body.
unsupported.stream.ndjson: apig-wsgi buffers the whole answer, so the rows arrive as one body.

skips.cors.vary: Flask-CORS writes Vary: Origin only when the policy allows more than one origin or a pattern, and settings.json names one origin.

noHandler.cors.preflight: Flask answers OPTIONS itself on every route, and Flask-CORS on the cors blueprint adds the policy to that answer. No view runs.
noHandler.errors.unmatched: Werkzeug's router answers a path no route matches with 404.
noHandler.errors.wrong_method: Werkzeug's router answers a method the path has no route for with 405.

authorized.mechanism: A before_request hook on the family's blueprint, which compares the bearer token Werkzeug parsed from the Authorization header and aborts with 403

baseline.builtin: The view returns the string with a text/plain content type.

body.mechanism: Flask-Pydantic's validate decorator, which binds the body to a Pydantic model before the view runs: types alone on the bind routes and orderRequest's rules on the validate routes. The first-error route's model checks the rules one field at a time, because Pydantic cannot stop at the first failure

cache.mechanism: Flask-Caching's cached decorator over a SimpleCache in each worker, which stores the response the view returned, keyed on the path and, for the vary rows, the headers the route varies on

compressed.mechanism: Flask-Compress's compressed decorator on the two views, at gzip's fastest level and Flask-Compress's default threshold

errors.builtin: Werkzeug's router answers a miss with 404 and a method a path lacks with 405, Flask refuses a body that is not JSON with 400, and the items views abort with 404, each as Werkzeug's HTML error page.

etag.mechanism: An after_request hook on the etag blueprint, which calls Werkzeug's add_etag and make_conditional on the response

forms.builtin: Werkzeug parses the form and the upload, and the view reads each value by name, converting the numbers as it reads them.

headers.builtin: Werkzeug's Headers, read by name, the account converted by get's type argument.

items.builtin: One view per method on /items/<int:id>, which Flask also answers HEAD with the GET view. Flask-Pydantic binds the bodies.

json.builtin: A view that returns a dict is answered by Flask's DefaultJSONProvider, over the standard library's json.

middleware.mechanism: One nested blueprint per layer count, each with that many no-op before_request hooks

parameters.builtin: Werkzeug's int converter on each capture.

query.builtin: Werkzeug's MultiDict.get, reading each value by name and converting the numbers.

sse.builtin: A generator of event text in a Response typed text/event-stream. Flask has no helper for server-sent events.

static.builtin: Flask's own static route, /static/<path:filename>, over the payload directory, which the application names as its static folder.

stream.builtin: A generator in a Response typed application/x-ndjson, which gunicorn sends chunked.

template.builtin: Flask's render_template, with the Jinja2 environment Flask builds for the application.
